newsitem.title: USA: Calif. counties blast Gov.'s veto of key tax bill.
newsitem.headline: Calif. counties blast Gov.'s veto of key tax bill.

text.p: The California State Association of Counties on Tuesday blasted Gov. Pete Wilson for vetoing legislation that would have changed local property tax allocations to benefit the state's local governments.
The measure would have prevented the property taxes taken by the state from counties and other local governments from growing beyond the amounts in fiscal year 1996-1997.

"It is deeply disturbing that the governor chose to perpetuate the financial crippling of California's counties, cities and special districts," said Mike Nevin, president of the California State Association of Counties.

"(Wilson) had the perfect opportunity to follow the lead of a virtually unanimous Legislature and begin to fix the horrible financial damage which the taking of $3.6 billion in property taxes has done to all local governments," Niven said.

Nearly $10 billion, or 54 percent, of the $19 billion in local property taxes collected goes to the state to balance its budget. This leaves about 20 percent of the property tax for counties and about 9.0 percent for cities, while the rest goes to special districts and redevelopment agencies, the association said in a statement.

Assembly Bill 2797 by Assemblyman Fred Aguiar and Senator William Craven was sponsored jointly by California State Association of Counties, the California Association of Realtors and the California Building Industry Association.
